correctness.rationale: Using H^2=1, H·E=0 and E^2=-1 gives beta=3F+E, c1=3H-E and c1·beta=7; the complex virtual dimension at one genus-zero mark is 7, matching psi^5 times the point. For the toric divisors (F,E,F,H) the pairings are (1,2,1,3). The z-normalized I-term has seven reciprocal factors, whose scalar parts contribute z^{-6}/(1!2!1!3!) after the leading z. For the mirror map compare the z^0 term in the z-normalization after separating the classical divisor exponential. The effective cone has generators E,F with anticanonical degrees 1,2. Terms of degree >=2 start at z^{-1} or below (a negative pairing lowers the power further through its m=0 factor). The only degree-one class is E, with pairings (1,-1,1,0); its term is zE/((F+z)(F+z)), also O(z^{-1}). Thus there is no positive-Novikov z^0 correction. By the projective toric mirror theorem the relevant small J has this coefficient, and expanding 1/(z-psi) identifies it at z^{-6} using that the Poincaré dual basis element to the identity is the point. This is an independent rederivation, not reliance on a historical status or the archived coefficient script.
